hero.title: Samudragupta: The Napoleon of India
hero.description: The greatest ruler of the Gupta dynasty, known for his relentless military conquests and multifaceted personality as a warrior-poet.

cards.details: Accession to the Gupta throne succeeding Chandragupta I.
Period of extensive military campaigns (Aryavarta and Dakshinapatha).

items.title: D.A.N.E
items.decryption: D: Dakshinapatha (Grahan-Moksha-Anugraha policy), A: Aryavarta (Nirmula policy/extermination), N: Nepalese/Frontier states (tribute), E: External powers (Kushan/Shaka relations).

items: Confusion: Samudragupta did not annex South India; he followed a policy of liberation (Moksha) after capturing kings.
Misconception: He is often called 'Napoleon' by V.A. Smith, not by ancient contemporaries.
Fact Check: He was a Vaishnava but practiced religious tolerance.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Core: Gangetic Plain
  • Dakshinapatha: Reached Kanchipuram
  • Frontier: Assam, Bengal, Nepal

Personalities

  • Harisena: Court Poet
  • Chandragupta I: Predecessor
  • Chandragupta II: Successor
  • Military Strategy
    • Aryavarta: Annexation (Direct control)
    • Dakshinapatha: Tributary (Indirect control)
    • Atavika Rajyas: Forest kingdoms subdued
  • Cultural Patronage
    • Kaviraja: Title for musical skill
    • Coinage: Veena-player type coins
    • Religious: Devotee of Vishnu but allowed Buddhist stupas
